condition: Find affordable products with useful features and positive customer feedback.

llm_config.evaluation_note: Discovery does not use human or LLM relevance labels.

signals.evidence: Review ratings directly indicate positive customer feedback, but do not provide evidence about product affordability or useful features.
Review summaries can provide direct textual evidence about customer feedback and product features, but the schema does not establish that they indicate affordability or positive sentiment.
Product.description may describe useful features, but it does not directly indicate affordability or positive customer feedback.
Product price directly relates to affordability, but does not indicate product features or customer feedback.
Review text is a direct source of customer feedback and may describe product features, but the schema does not establish positive sentiment or product affordability.
A product title may indicate its type or advertised features, but it does not directly establish affordability or positive customer feedback.
Product brand may provide weak indirect context, but it does not directly indicate affordability, useful features, or customer feedback.
Product category may indirectly indicate the kind of features a product offers, but it does not directly show affordability or positive customer feedback.
Review time is weakly relevant as temporal context for customer feedback, but it does not indicate whether feedback is positive or whether products are affordable or have useful features.
A verified review may add credibility to customer feedback, but it does not indicate whether the feedback is positive or address product affordability or features.
Customer names provide no schema-grounded evidence about product affordability, features, or positive feedback.

condition: Show detailed reviews describing real-world product experiences.

llm_config.evaluation_note: Discovery does not use human or LLM relevance labels.

signals.evidence: review.review_text directly contains review content, making it strong evidence for identifying detailed descriptions of real-world product experiences.
A verified review is evidence of a real-world product experience, but verified status does not indicate whether the review is detailed.
The review summary is directly associated with each review and may indicate its topic, but it is less direct evidence of detailed real-world experiences than review_text.
Product category can provide weak context for which products reviews concern, but it does not indicate review detail or real-world experiences.
A product description gives context about the product, but does not indicate whether reviews describe real-world experiences.
A product title can identify which product reviews concern, but it does not indicate whether reviews are detailed or describe real-world experiences.
The review rating can indicate an overall evaluation, but it does not show whether the review describes detailed real-world experiences.
Product price may provide purchase context, but it does not indicate review detail or real-world experience.
Brand identifies the product, but does not indicate whether its reviews are detailed or describe real-world experiences.
Review time may help prioritize recent experiences, but it does not indicate whether a review is detailed or describes real-world product use.
Customer name may identify who wrote a review, but it does not indicate whether the review is detailed or describes real-world product experiences.

condition: Find reliable products from reputable brands with strong customer ratings.

llm_config.evaluation_note: Discovery does not use human or LLM relevance labels.

signals.evidence: Review ratings directly indicate customer ratings, but do not establish product reliability or brand reputation.
Product.brand directly supports the reputable-brand aspect, but the schema does not define reputation, and brand alone does not provide customer ratings or reliability evidence.
A verified review may provide indirect evidence that customer feedback is trustworthy, but it does not indicate the product’s rating or brand reputation.
A product description may provide indirect clues about reliability, but it does not directly encode brand reputation or customer ratings.
Review text may contain customer feedback relevant to product reliability, but it does not directly provide ratings or brand reputation.
A review summary may provide indirect customer feedback relevant to reliability, but it does not directly identify brand reputation or rating strength.
Product category can provide indirect product context, but it does not indicate brand reputation, reliability, or customer ratings.
The product title can identify a product, but the schema does not indicate that it provides evidence of brand reputation, reliability, or customer ratings.
Review time may provide weak temporal context for a review, but it does not directly indicate ratings, product reliability, or brand reputation.
Product price is available, but it does not directly indicate brand reputation, product reliability, or customer ratings.
Customer names provide no schema-grounded evidence about product brands, ratings, or reliability.

condition: Find negative reviews highlighting defects, poor quality, or disappointing performance.

llm_config.evaluation_note: Discovery does not use human or LLM relevance labels.

signals.evidence: review.review_text directly contains the review content needed to identify complaints about defects, poor quality, or disappointing performance.
A review summary can concisely describe defects, poor quality, or disappointing performance, but it may omit the negative sentiment or specific issue.

A review's rating can indicate negative sentiment and help identify potentially negative reviews, but it does not reveal whether the review highlights defects, poor quality, or disappointing performance.
Product brand may indirectly group reviews by manufacturer, but it does not directly indicate negative sentiment, defects, quality, or performance.
Product category can provide weak context for the types of defects or performance concerns relevant to a product, but it does not indicate whether any review is negative.
Product descriptions may provide context for judging performance claims, but they do not directly indicate whether reviews are negative or mention defects or poor quality.
Product price may provide indirect context for expectations, but it does not directly identify negative reviews or defects, poor quality, or disappointing performance.
A product title may help identify the product being reviewed, but the schema provides no indication that it signals defects, poor quality, or disappointing performance.
review.verified indicates whether a review is verified, but does not directly identify negative sentiment, defects, poor quality, or disappointing performance.
Customer names provide no direct evidence of negative sentiment, defects, poor quality, or performance.
Review time does not indicate whether a review is negative or mentions defects, poor quality, or disappointing performance.

condition: Identify customers who write thoughtful, balanced, and informative reviews.

llm_config.evaluation_note: Discovery does not use human or LLM relevance labels.

signals.evidence: Review text directly indicates whether a review is thoughtful, balanced, and informative, but this signal’s path does not link reviews to customers.
A review summary may provide some evidence of informative content, but it is not the full review text and does not capture the customer relationship needed to identify reviewers.

Product category can provide context for the subject of a customer's review through the review–product relationship, but it does not indicate whether the review is thoughtful, balanced, or informative.
A review rating indicates the reviewer’s evaluation, but does not show whether the review is thoughtful, balanced, or informative.
The verified attribute may weakly indicate review credibility, but it does not directly describe whether a review is thoughtful, balanced, or informative.
The product title can provide context about what was reviewed, but it does not indicate whether the review is thoughtful, balanced, or informative, or identify its author.
Customer name identifies the customer but provides no schema-based evidence about whether their reviews are thoughtful, balanced, or informative.
Product brand is not schema-linked to review quality or customer writing behavior.
Product.description provides product context but the stated path does not connect to reviews or customers, so it offers no direct evidence about who writes thoughtful, balanced, informative reviews.
Product price is not a review attribute and provides no schema-grounded evidence about whether a customer’s reviews are thoughtful, balanced, or informative.
review_time records when a review was written, but does not indicate whether its content is thoughtful, balanced, or informative.

condition: Find products that are similar in their purpose, features, and the needs they address, even when their descriptions use different terminology.

llm_config.evaluation_note: Discovery does not use human or LLM relevance labels.

signals.evidence: Product descriptions directly provide information about purpose, features, and needs that can support semantic similarity despite differing terminology.

Product category provides direct but coarse evidence of product purpose; it may group products addressing similar needs, but does not capture detailed features or semantic similarities across different categories.
Review text can describe product features, uses, and needs addressed, supporting semantic comparison, but it is indirect evidence and the schema does not guarantee that reviews cover these aspects.
A product title can convey its type or intended use, offering some evidence for similarity, but titles may omit features and needs or use different terminology.
Product price may weakly indicate product tier or intended use, but it does not directly capture purpose, features, or needs, especially across different terminology.
Review summaries may mention product purposes or features in varied language, but they are review-level text and the stated path does not connect them to product attributes.
A product’s brand may weakly indicate related product lines, but brand alone does not describe its purpose, features, or the needs it addresses.
Review ratings may weakly indicate user evaluations, but they do not describe product purpose, features, or needs addressed.
Review verification may weakly indicate review credibility, but it does not describe product purpose, features, or needs addressed.
Customer names provide no schema-grounded evidence about products’ purposes, features, or needs addressed.
Review time provides no schema-grounded evidence about product purpose, features, or needs addressed.

condition: Find products that appeal to similar groups of customers based on their purchasing and reviewing behavior, even if the products belong to different categories.

llm_config.evaluation_note: Discovery does not use human or LLM relevance labels.

signals.evidence: Review text can reveal expressed preferences and interests useful for comparing reviewing behavior, but this signal alone does not connect reviews to customers or products.
Review summaries can indicate what reviewers value, providing evidence about reviewing preferences, but this signal alone does not connect reviews to customer groups or capture purchasing behavior.
Review ratings provide direct evidence of customer responses, but the signal does not include customer or product links needed to identify overlapping customer groups across products.
Product descriptions may indirectly indicate products with similar appeal, but they do not capture customer purchasing or reviewing behavior.
Product price may weakly indicate the kinds of customers a product attracts, but it does not capture purchasing or reviewing behavior or link products to shared customers.
Product titles may provide indirect clues for comparing products across categories, but they do not capture customer purchasing or reviewing behavior or identify similar customer groups.
Review time may weakly indicate when customers review products, but this signal does not connect reviews to customers or products, so it provides little evidence about shared customer groups.
Review verification status offers weak evidence about reviewing behavior, but does not link reviews to customers or products or directly reveal customer-group similarity.
Product category provides product context, but does not capture customer purchasing or reviewing behavior and may not connect products across categories.
Brand identifies a product attribute that may weakly group products, but it does not capture customer purchasing or reviewing behavior.
Customer name identifies a customer but provides no direct evidence of their purchasing or reviewing behavior or of products appealing to similar customer groups.

condition: Find customer reviews that provide detailed, credible, and useful insights into a product's strengths, weaknesses, and real-world performance.

llm_config.evaluation_note: Discovery does not use human or LLM relevance labels.

signals.evidence: Review text directly contains the review content and can provide detailed descriptions of product strengths, weaknesses, and real-world performance; credibility is not guaranteed by this attribute alone.
review.verified is relevant to credibility, but it does not indicate whether a review is detailed or discusses strengths, weaknesses, or real-world performance.
A review summary may indicate whether it discusses product strengths, weaknesses, or performance, but it may omit the detail needed to assess usefulness and credibility.
A review rating provides an overall assessment that may indicate positive or negative product experiences, but it does not reveal detailed strengths, weaknesses, or credibility.
Product category can provide context for interpreting reviews, but it does not indicate whether they are detailed, credible, or useful, or describe strengths and weaknesses.
Product.description can provide context for interpreting review claims, but it does not indicate whether reviews are detailed, credible, or describe real-world performance.
Product price may provide context for judging a review’s value-for-money insights, but it does not directly indicate review detail, credibility, strengths, weaknesses, or real-world performance.
The product title can identify the product whose reviews are sought, but it provides no evidence that reviews are detailed, credible, or useful.

Review time provides temporal context for assessing how current a review is, but it does not indicate detail, credibility, or whether the review discusses product strengths, weaknesses, or performance.
Product brand provides context for the reviewed product but does not indicate whether a review is detailed, credible, or useful.
Customer names do not indicate review detail, credibility, usefulness, or product performance.

condition: Find products that offer particularly good value for money by balancing affordability, perceived quality, and customer satisfaction.

llm_config.evaluation_note: Discovery does not use human or LLM relevance labels.

signals.evidence: Product price directly indicates affordability, but alone does not capture perceived quality or customer satisfaction.
Review ratings directly indicate perceived quality and customer satisfaction, but this path provides no price evidence for assessing affordability.
Review text can provide qualitative evidence of perceived quality and customer satisfaction, but it does not provide product affordability or price.
Review summaries can provide qualitative evidence of perceived quality and satisfaction, but they do not indicate affordability or explicitly connect the signal to products.
Product.description may provide indirect evidence about features or quality, but it does not directly capture affordability or customer satisfaction.
Brand is a direct product attribute and may offer weak context for perceived quality, but the schema does not connect it to price, ratings, or customer satisfaction.
Product category provides context for comparing value within a product type, but does not directly indicate affordability, perceived quality, or customer satisfaction.
Review time can indicate how recent customer feedback is, but it does not directly signal affordability, perceived quality, or satisfaction.
A verified review may provide more credible evidence about customer satisfaction, but it does not directly indicate affordability, perceived quality, or satisfaction level.
A product title identifies the product and may offer limited contextual clues, but it does not directly indicate affordability, perceived quality, or customer satisfaction.
Customer names provide no schema-grounded evidence about product affordability, perceived quality, or customer satisfaction.

condition: Find customers who have similar preferences and expectations, as reflected in the products they review, the opinions they express, and the aspects of products they care about.

llm_config.evaluation_note: Discovery does not use human or LLM relevance labels.

signals.evidence: Review text directly captures customers’ expressed opinions and product aspects they care about, but does not by itself represent the products reviewed or connect reviews to customers.

Review summaries can directly capture expressed opinions and product aspects, providing useful evidence for comparing preferences, but they do not alone establish similarity across customers or identify the products reviewed.
Product brand can reveal shared brand preferences among customers through the products they review, but it does not capture their expressed opinions or the product aspects they care about.
Product descriptions can reveal product attributes and aspects relevant to customer preferences, but this signal alone does not connect products to customers or capture their opinions.
Product price can provide evidence about customers’ price preferences through the products they review, but it does not capture their expressed opinions or other product aspects.
Product titles can indicate the kinds of products customers review, offering useful but incomplete preference evidence; they do not capture expressed opinions or specific aspects of interest.

Review ratings directly reflect opinions and can provide partial evidence of preferences, but the signal does not include the reviewed products, expressed aspects, or a path connecting reviews to customers.

Product category can provide a broad signal of product preferences, but this signal’s stated path does not connect categories to the customers who reviewed those products or capture their opinions and specific product aspects.
Review time can provide indirect temporal context for a customer's reviews, but it does not directly capture reviewed products, expressed opinions, or product aspects.
Review verification may indicate how much to trust an opinion, but it does not directly describe the customer's preferences, reviewed products, or product aspects they care about.
The customer name does not indicate reviewed products, expressed opinions, or product aspects of interest.

condition: I'm looking for products that serve similar purposes, regardless of their brand or category.

llm_config.evaluation_note: Discovery does not use human or LLM relevance labels.

signals.evidence: Product.description can provide direct information about a product’s purpose, supporting similarity comparisons without relying on brand or category.
A product title can describe what the product is for, supporting purpose-based similarity without relying on brand or category.
Review text may mention a product’s use or purpose, but it is indirect and the schema does not guarantee that reviews describe this.
Review summaries may mention a product’s use or purpose, but they are review text rather than direct product-purpose attributes, so the evidence is weak and indirect.
Product category may weakly suggest purpose, but the condition explicitly seeks similarity regardless of category, so this signal should not constrain matches.
Product price may weakly reflect a product’s market segment, but it does not directly indicate its purpose.
Customer names provide no schema-grounded evidence about products’ purposes or similarity.
Brand is explicitly irrelevant to the condition, and the schema does not indicate that it captures product purpose.
A review rating provides no schema-grounded evidence about product purpose or similarity.
Review time gives no schema-grounded evidence about a product’s purpose or similarity.
review.verified indicates whether a review is verified, but does not describe product purpose or similarity.

condition: Which products appeal to similar customers based on their reviewing behavior?

llm_config.evaluation_note: Discovery does not use human or LLM relevance labels.

signals.evidence: Review text can express customer opinions and preferences, providing behavioral evidence, but this signal alone does not connect reviews to customers or products.
Review ratings directly reflect customers’ evaluations, which can inform product appeal, but this signal alone does not identify which customers reviewed which products or establish similarity.
Review timestamps can provide a temporal aspect of customers’ reviewing behavior, but this signal alone does not link reviews to customers or products.
Customer names can identify customers, but the signal contains no review behavior or product association.
Brand can weakly group products, but it provides no direct evidence about which customers reviewed them or whether their reviewing behavior is similar.
Product category can group products by type, but it does not capture which customers reviewed them or whether their reviewing behavior is similar.
Product descriptions may indicate product similarity, but they do not capture which customers reviewed the products or their reviewing behavior.
Product price may weakly indicate product similarity, but it does not capture which customers review products or their reviewing behavior.
Product title can identify which products are being compared, but it provides no evidence about the customers who review them or their reviewing behavior.
Review summaries may indicate topics or preferences expressed in reviews, but this signal has no customer or product relationship path to connect that behavior to particular customers or products.
The verified flag provides a limited review-level behavior signal, but it does not identify customers, products, or similarity between them.

condition: Show me reviews that provide useful insights into a product's strengths and weaknesses.

llm_config.evaluation_note: Discovery does not use human or LLM relevance labels.

signals.evidence: Review text is a direct source of written feedback that may describe a product’s strengths and weaknesses.
A review’s summary is directly associated with the review and can provide concise evidence about product strengths and weaknesses; its actual content is not specified.
A review rating can indicate overall positive or negative sentiment, helping identify reviews relevant to strengths or weaknesses, but it does not specify what those are.
Product category provides context about the kind of product, but does not indicate whether its reviews describe strengths or weaknesses.
A product description can provide context for interpreting a review’s comments about strengths and weaknesses, but it does not directly indicate whether a review contains useful insights.
Product price may provide context for reviews discussing value, but it does not directly indicate whether a review describes strengths or weaknesses.
A review’s verified status may weakly indicate credibility, but it does not directly show whether the review discusses product strengths or weaknesses.
Brand identifies the product's maker, but does not indicate whether its reviews discuss strengths or weaknesses.
A product title can identify the product being reviewed, but it does not indicate whether review content discusses strengths or weaknesses.
Review time may weakly indicate recency, but it does not show whether the review discusses a product’s strengths or weaknesses.
Customer names provide no schema-grounded evidence about whether a review describes a product’s strengths or weaknesses.

condition: Prioritize products that offer a good balance of price, quality, and customer satisfaction.

llm_config.evaluation_note: Discovery does not use human or LLM relevance labels.

signals.evidence: Review ratings directly indicate customer satisfaction and may provide an imperfect quality signal, but they do not capture product price.
Product price directly informs the price side of the requested balance, but alone provides no evidence about quality or customer satisfaction.
Review text can provide evidence about perceived product quality and customer satisfaction, but this signal contains no price information to assess the balance.
Review summaries can provide qualitative evidence of customer satisfaction and perceived quality, but they do not directly encode product price or establish a product-level balance.
Brand is a product attribute that may help distinguish products, but it does not directly indicate price, quality, or customer satisfaction.
Product category can provide context for comparing products within a category, but it does not directly indicate price, quality, or customer satisfaction.
Product description may provide indirect evidence about quality or features, but it does not directly indicate price or customer satisfaction.
Review time can provide temporal context for customer feedback, but it does not directly indicate product price, quality, or satisfaction.
A review’s verified status may modestly indicate the credibility of customer feedback, but it does not directly measure satisfaction, product quality, or price.
Product titles identify products but do not directly indicate price, quality, or customer satisfaction.
Customer names do not provide schema evidence about product price, quality, or customer satisfaction.

condition: I'd like to discover customers with similar tastes based on their ratings and opinions.

llm_config.evaluation_note: Discovery does not use human or LLM relevance labels.

signals.evidence: Review ratings directly indicate customers’ expressed evaluations and can support comparing tastes across reviews, though this signal alone omits written opinions and customer associations.
Review text directly captures customers’ expressed opinions, but this review-only signal does not connect reviews to customers or include ratings.
Review summaries can capture opinions relevant to taste similarity, but this signal alone does not include ratings or a path to identify customers.
Product brand can indicate a shared preference dimension, but this signal alone does not connect products to customers or include their ratings and opinions.
Product category can weakly indicate the kinds of items relevant to customer tastes, but this signal has no path to reviews or customers and does not capture ratings or opinions.
Product descriptions can provide indirect semantic evidence about the items customers may like, but this signal alone does not capture customer ratings, opinions, or the customer-review associations.
Product price may weakly reflect a price-related preference, but it does not capture ratings or opinions and the stated path does not connect the signal to customers.
Product titles can identify items whose reviews might indicate shared tastes, but the signal alone provides no customer associations, ratings, or opinions.
Review verification may weakly indicate the reliability of an opinion, but it does not capture ratings or opinion content needed to identify similar tastes.
Review time may weakly indicate when customers reviewed products, but it does not directly capture the ratings or opinions that define similar tastes.
Customer name does not indicate ratings or opinions, and the signal path reaches no review data.
